subject: Platform health gate + QBR readouts (Sep 2028)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Emma Clarke <emma@acme.io>
Date: 2028-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Platform health gate + QBR readouts (Sep 2028)

Team / Emma — attaching the Sep month KPI bundle we plan to present at the QBR. High-level callouts I want on the radar before the dry-run: 

- Latency: sharp 350ms p95 spike on 2028-09-05 during the canary rollout (attached annotated screenshot).
- Cost: Serving tier B overspend vs. forecast (~18% over run-rate) driven by unexpected retry amplification on multi-tenant endpoints.
- Uptime: brief 22-minute degradation on 2028-09-07 during a control-plane migration; customer-facing signals were recovered via automatic fallback but we need a clearer RCA.
- Usage: steady month-over-month growth +21% for inference tokens; this will be a positive talking point for execs but it stresses autoscaling margins.

Asks: please confirm owners for the QBR deep-dives: Markus on latency RCA + mitigation plan, Irene on uptime/control-plane safeguards and audit notes, Jonas on usage/cost narrative + short-term mitigations. Emma — any specific slides you want us to expand?

Action timeline: owners to send 1-slide owner notes and any pre-read updates by 2028-09-14 EOD. Dry-run scheduled for 2028-09-20 10:00 PT.

Attachments: sep-2028-kpi-dashboard.pdf (PDF, 18 pages), latency-spike-annotated.png (PNG), cost-runbook-v1.docx (DOCX, stub)

Thanks,
Tessa
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-13T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform health gate + QBR readouts (Sep 2028)

Tessa — got it, I'm taking the latency RCA. Quick notes: 

- Initial hypothesis: GPU kernel miscompile during the canary (driver + kernel mismatch) combined with a workload shift (longer avg sequence length) caused cache fragmentation and higher scheduling latency.
- Immediate ask: can we get token-level breakout for the spike window (2028-09-05 14:00–15:30 PT)? I want the per-model p95 and the KV cache hit rate in that window.
- Short-term mitigation I propose: revert the canary kernel on affected pools and enable aggressive KV-cache warming for the next 48 hours.

If those look good I'll draft a single-slide RCA + follow-ups and add a small runbook trigger (Ops-1248).

On Wed, Sep 12, Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Team / Emma — attaching the Sep month KPI bundle we plan to present at the QBR...

-Markus

From: Emma Clarke <emma@acme.io>

Date: 2028-09-14T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Platform health gate + QBR readouts (Sep 2028)

Thanks, Tessa. A couple quick clarifications from the customer side: 

- Can you confirm whether traffic for our prod tenant fell back to the Regional fallback pool during the 09-07 outage? We saw a brief increase in error rates and want to correlate with your control-plane event.
- For the latency spike on 09-05, do you have the per-model p95 available (we run three active model versions)? If not, an approximate breakdown helps.

I've attached a short screenshot from our monitoring that shows the error spike (ops-screenshot-0907.png). Happy to join the dry-run if useful.

— Emma
